retrieval_candidates.name: verify_temporal_resolution_for_transient_pathology
retrieval_candidates.description: When initial imaging shows diffuse bilateral opacities, verify if findings resolve rapidly in follow-up images to distinguish transient conditions from persistent pathologies.
retrieval_candidates.applicable_conditions: Tasks involving the interpretation of serial medical imaging where the differential diagnosis includes both transient (e.g., hemorrhage, edema) and persistent (e.g., infection, fibrosis) causes of similar radiographic appearances.
retrieval_candidates.body:
### Core Action
If the initial image analysis reveals high-confidence diffuse bilateral opacities: (1) explicitly retrieve and analyze available follow-up imaging using `chest_xray_classifier`; (2) compare the severity and extent of findings between the initial and follow-up timepoints; (3) if findings show rapid normalization or significant improvement, prioritize transient etiologies (e.g., hemorrhage, flash pulmonary edema) over slower-resolving pathologies (e.g., pneumonia, ARDS) in the final diagnosis.

retrieval_candidates.name: verify_negative_classifier_with_visual_morphology
retrieval_candidates.description: When a chest X-ray classifier returns no strong findings despite visible pathology, perform direct visual inspection of morphological features and temporal stability to identify chronic or congenital conditions.
retrieval_candidates.applicable_conditions: Chest imaging interpretation tasks where automated classification tools yield negative or low-confidence results for images containing obvious structural abnormalities.
retrieval_candidates.body:
### Core Action
If `chest_xray_classifier` returns empty `strong_findings` but clinical suspicion for structural pathology (e.g., calcification, pericardial thickening, effusion, mass) remains high: (1) Do not accept the negative classifier output as final; (2) Explicitly invoke `chest_xray_report_generator` to analyze specific views (especially lateral) for morphological details (e.g., curvilinear calcifications, silhouette abnormalities) and obtain radiologist-style interpretations; (3) Formulate diagnosis and inform treatment planning based on the generated report rather than relying on internal visual inspection or the initial classifier's strong findings. CRITICAL PRECONDITION CHECK: This skill MUST NOT be invoked if `chest_xray_classifier` has already returned non-empty `strong_findings`. In cases with positive classifier findings, prioritize those findings and use visual morphology only for refinement or confirmation, not to override explicit positive detections with negative-verification logic.

retrieval_candidates.name: verify_bilateral_hilar_findings_with_lateral_view
retrieval_candidates.description: When a chest X-ray classifier identifies high-confidence masses in bilateral hilar regions, verify the finding using lateral views to distinguish symmetric adenopathy from malignancy.
retrieval_candidates.applicable_conditions: Chest imaging tasks where automated classifiers detect bilateral hilar abnormalities or masses, requiring differentiation between lymphadenopathy (e.g., sarcoidosis) and neoplastic processes.
retrieval_candidates.body:
### Core Action
If `chest_xray_classifier` returns a high-confidence 'Mass' finding for bilateral hilar structures: (1) Do not accept the label as definitive malignancy; (2) Call `chest_xray_report_generator` specifically on lateral views; (3) Analyze the report for symmetry of hilar enlargement and absence of parenchymal invasion; (4) Prioritize the morphological pattern of symmetric adenopathy over the generic classifier label if lateral view confirms symmetry.

retrieval_candidates.name: temporal_severity_quantification
retrieval_candidates.description: When evaluating the evolution of chest pathology over time, explicitly quantify severity changes using a classifier on serial images rather than relying on visual estimation.
retrieval_candidates.applicable_conditions: Tasks involving the interpretation of multiple chest imaging studies (e.g., X-rays, CTs) taken at different time points to assess disease progression, resolution, or stability.
retrieval_candidates.body:
### Core Action
When analyzing temporal chest imaging sequences to distinguish transient from persistent pathology: (1) Identify key timepoints (e.g., baseline, peak severity, current/resolution); (2) Invoke `chest_xray_classifier` on each selected image to obtain objective severity scores; (3) Compare the quantitative outputs to determine the trajectory (improving, worsening, stable) rather than relying on subjective visual comparison alone.
